rendering.persona_description: Rohan is 24 and works as an assistant manager at a hardware store in the town where he grew up. He's close with his mother and still calls her most nights, and he's had the same dog, a beagle named Chip, since high school. He likes fixing small engines in his spare time and used to coach a rec-league soccer team for kids until he quietly stepped back from it last year.
rendering.clinical_context: Rohan has OCD with harm-themed intrusive thoughts, most often images of hurting his mother or his dog with a knife or with his hands. The thoughts started about three years ago after he read a news story about a man who attacked his own family, and he was diagnosed with OCD roughly eighteen months ago. He started a course of exposure and response prevention about four months ago but has been thinking about stopping because he doesn't believe the exercises are proving anything about whether he's actually dangerous.
rendering.behavioral_description: Rohan talks in a careful, worried way, laying out specific incidents like evidence in a case he's building against himself. He asks pointed questions meant to get a read on whether he's a risk, and he'll push back, sometimes for several exchanges, if someone tells him the thoughts don't mean anything, because to him that skips over the part where he has to actually rule it out. He'll consider a suggestion if it's framed as another way to check the facts, but he's suspicious of anything that sounds like it's just supposed to make him feel calmer.
